title: Eagle-Eye Shields's band from Jacksonville
summary: The small Jacksonville band that came through Savannah, and the later story of Edmund Hall and Cootie Williams's mother.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: There was a band out of Jacksonville, Florida used to come through there. It was Eagle-Eye Shields band. He has a son today that plays drums around Las Vegas and places like that. And I see him. I often think of his father, you know. But his name was -- he played piano and his name was Eagle-Eye Shields. But he was originally from Savannah, but he went to Jacksonville and he had a good bank together. At --

About six. Bands were -- no bands in those days had over six or seven pieces. If you had eight, nine pieces you had a real big band in those days. But they were five, six pieces -- like that because later on Edmund
Hall played with Eagle-Eye Shields, and so did -- so did Cootie Williams. This is way back.

Edmund Hall was telling me that story how he had to talk to Cootie Williams' mother. Cootie lived in Mobile, and Edmund was from down New Orleans, see, and how he had to talk to his mother to get her -- get them to let Cootie down there and play for him. When I worked with Edmund with Louis he was talking about this story.
